assumptions: All 398 VMs priced as steady-state workloads using 1-Year Compute Savings Plan (No Upfront) - cost-optimized for continuous operation
Region ap-south-1 (Asia Pacific Mumbai) used for all instances per primary region instruction
All locations (India/Bangalore/Adelaide/Calgary) mapped to ap-south-1 as the single target region

Instance family selection: c6a for AMD+c6i-recommended, c6i for Intel+c6i-recommended, m6a for AMD+m6i-recommended, m6i for Intel+m6i-recommended, r6a for AMD+r6i-recommended, r6i for Intel+r6i-recommended
Instance size = smallest in recommended family fitting both Sized vCPU AND Sized RAM
Storage per instance = representative average for that group (gp3 SSD)
No data transfer, no detailed monitoring, no snapshot storage (not specified in workbook)
Row 91 (Finance Server Tally): 1vCPU/512GB RAM → r6i.32xlarge (1024GB, smallest fitting 512GB RAM)
Row 400 (TOTAL row) excluded as non-billable header
Rows 185-320 (172.16.5.163 cluster) have OS Family 'Linux/Other' despite version numbers like '2019','2022' - priced as Linux per OS Family column
Rows 382-390 (Bekhoff servers) have Storage=0 - priced as c6i.large with minimal storage; zero-storage rows still incur compute cost
Storage amounts per group set to representative median for that instance group
warnings: Row 91: RAM=512GB is very unusual for a VM migration. r6i.32xlarge (1024GB) is the minimum r6i instance fitting 512GB RAM - this is extremely expensive. Customer should verify this is intentional.

Rows 185-320 OS Family is 'Linux/Other' but Guest OS shows Windows version names (2019, 2022, 2016, 2012r2). Priced as Linux per the OS Family column. If these are Windows, cost will be significantly higher.
Row 173: 80vCPU/32GB - extremely high vCPU count for a single VM. Priced on c6i.32xlarge. Customer should verify.

Due to the 398-VM scope, VMs were consolidated into 48 EC2 calculator entries grouped by instance type and OS. Individual VM storage amounts are averaged/representative within each group. For per-VM precision, each row would need a separate entry.
Compute Savings Plans under shared tenancy are the closest AWS Calculator equivalent to Standard Reserved Instances (which require dedicated/host tenancy in the Calculator).

The workbook 'service hint: Backup' was found to contain only VM/compute inventory rows (rows 369-399 are physical desktops and Bekhoff servers) - no AWS Backup service rows were found; all rows priced as EC2.
